Failure behaviors in SS 347H Molten Salt Hot Tanks [4]. 1.3 Project Description and Approach The first phase of the project consisted of Tasks 1 through 5 (see Figure 2), whose primary goal was understanding the mechanical failure mechanisms in commercial-scale molten salt TES tanks. The second phase of the project focused on analyzing the impact of tank size and the tank preheating process (Tasks 6 and 7) on the stress and deformation distributions in the tank, particularly in the tank floor. This project was divided into seven tasks and seven milestones. A detailed diagram showing the tasks, activities, and milestones is presented in Figure 2. Milestones 1 through 5, which were associated with Tasks 1 to 5, were described in the previous project report [4]. The project team developed a representative molten salt hot tank design based on information received from multiple CSP plants, see Figure 3. This design considered high-level dimensions characteristic of tanks with a capacity of 100 MW or larger. Although the representative design applies to multiple plants, it does not fully correspond to any particular plant, ensuring the confidentiality of the proprietary information received. After the representative tank geometry was created in Solid Edge and transferred to ANSYS, the resulting model was optimized and validated using historical operational data. Simulations were conducted using NLR’s Eagle and Kestrel high-performance computers (HPC). Since the proprietary data could not be used directly, the team developed a unique dataset of representative operational cases. The complete hot tank model is an integrated simulation system built from four sequential sub-models to analyze the thermal and structural performance of TES tanks. The process begins with the sparger ring computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model, which uses the incoming salt flow conditions (from the downcomer) to predict the flow rates exiting the sparger orifices. These rates then serve as boundary conditions for the CFD molten salt inventory model, implemented in ANSYS, which simulates the salt mixing process within the tank and determines the resulting temperature and pressure distributions throughout the salt and tank at every timestep. The thermal data is then transferred to the tank mechanical (structural) model to calculate the associated thermal stress induced in the tank's floor, shell, and roof.
